arxiv-2207-13724.creator: Jing Zhou, Zhi-Yu Zhang, Yu Gao, Junzhi Wang, Yong Shi, Qiusheng Gu, Chentao Yang, Tao Wang, Qing-Hua Tan
arxiv-2207-13724.description: Abstract Both Galactic and extragalactic studies on star formation suggest that stars form directly from dense molecular gas. To trace such high volume density gas, HCN and HCO + J = 1 → 0 J=1\rightarrow 0 have been widely used for their high dipole moments, relatively high abundances, and often being the strongest lines after CO.

arxiv-2212-10125.title: B B meson Decay Constants Using Relativistic Heavy Quarks
arxiv-2212-10125.creator: Oliver Witzel
arxiv-2212-10125.description: Abstract We present an update on ongoing work to extract pseudoscalar and vector decay constants for B ( ∗ ) B^{(*)} , B s ( ∗ ) B^{(*)}_{s} and B c ( ∗ ) B^{(*)}_{c} mesons and determine phenomenologically-interesting ratios such as f B s / f B f_{B_{s}}/f_{B} or f B ∗ / f B f_{B^{*}}/f_{B} .

arxiv-2310-02965.title: Structure transition and zigzag magnetic order in Ir/Rh-substituted honeycomb lattice α \alpha -RuCl 3
arxiv-2310-02965.creator: Zachary Morgan, Iris Ye, Colin L. Sarkis, Xiaoping Wang, Stephen Nagler, Jiaqiang Yan
arxiv-2310-02965.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Zachary Morgan, Iris Ye, Colin L. Sarkis, Xiaoping Wang, Stephen Nagler, Jiaqiang Yan. We report magnetization and neutron diffraction studies on crystal and magnetic structures of Ir- and Rh-substituted honeycomb lattice α \alpha -RuCl 3 . The iridium or rhodium atoms are distributed at the Ru site with little structural modification. Both systems undergo a room-temperature monoclinic C ​ 2 / m C2/m to low-temperature trigonal R ​ 3 ¯ R\bar{3} phase transformation with a large recoverable hysteresis.

arxiv-2501-06161.title: RIOT-based smart metering system for privacy-preserving data aggregation using watermarking and encryption
arxiv-2501-06161.creator: Farzana Kabir 1, David Megías 1, Krzysztof Cabaj 2
arxiv-2501-06161.description: Abstract The remarkable advancement of smart grid technology in the IoT sector has raised concerns over the privacy and security of the data collected and transferred in real-time. Smart meters generate detailed information about consumers’ energy consumption patterns, increasing the risks of data breaches, identity theft, and other forms of cyber attacks.

arxiv-2508-16756.description: Abstract We present detailed radio observations of the mid-infrared (MIR) tidal disruption event (TDE) WTP14adeqka. We detect rising radio emission starting ≈ 4 \approx 4 years after the discovery of the MIR emission (and about 2 years after its peak), peaking at ≈ 6.5 \approx 6.

arxiv-2509-09825.title: Surface Topological Quantum Criticality II: Conformal manifolds, Isolated fixed points, and Entanglement
arxiv-2509-09825.creator: Saran Vijayan, Fei Zhou
arxiv-2509-09825.description: Abstract In this article, we propose a possibility of realizing conformal manifolds, which are smooth manifolds of scale-conformal invariant interacting Hamiltonians in two-dimensional quantum many-body systems. Such phenomena can occur in various interacting systems, including topological surfaces or 2D bulks.

arxiv-2602-18683.title: Nucleon Size Independence of Hadronic Nucleus-Nucleus Cross Sections
arxiv-2602-18683.creator: Hao-jie Xu
arxiv-2602-18683.description: Abstract Recent proposals to constrain the nucleon size using hadronic cross sections ( σ AA \sigma_{\rm AA} ) conflict with collective flow data. I demonstrate this dependence is an artifact of “geometric inflation,” where smearing point-like nucleons unintentionally dilutes the nuclear surface.

arxiv-2603-07941.title: Terahertz-nanoscale visualization of the microscopic spin-charge architecture of colossal magnetoresistive switching

pmc-11659975.title: Significance of eGFR and proteinuria for cardiovascular disease in individuals beyond 85 years of age
pmc-11659975.creator: Tatsuhiko Azegami, Hidehiro Kaneko, Akira Okada, Yuta Suzuki, Katsuhito Fujiu, Hiroyuki Morita, Norifumi Takeda, Norihiko Takeda, Akira Fukui, Takashi Yokoo, Koichi Node, Hideo Yasunaga, Masaomi Nangaku, Kaori Hayashi
pmc-11659975.description: BackgroundThere are limited data on how advancing age influences prediction of cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk based on the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and proteinuria, especially in older adults, including those aged ≥85 years old. This study aimed to clarify the association of eGFR and proteinuria with CVD outcomes and the impact of age on this association.

pmc-12565062.title: Chronic Insomnia and Stroke Risk—A Real Bidirectional Issue
pmc-12565062.creator: Brindusa Ilinca Mitoiu, Maria Delia Alexe, Gavril Lucian Gheorghievici, Roxana Nartea, Katalin Prokai-Tatrai, Gelu Onose, Constantin Munteanu
pmc-12565062.description: Chronic insomnia is a prevalent and disabling sleep disorder with growing evidence linking it to cardiovascular and cerebrovascular morbidity. Stroke, a leading cause of mortality and a long-term disability worldwide, may be influenced by sleep disturbances through multiple physiological mechanisms.

pmc-12639215.title: Rehabilitation of the Knee After Autologous Matrix-Induced Chondrogenesis: A Systematic Review of Rehabilitation Protocols and Clinical and Radiological Outcomes
pmc-12639215.creator: Jonathan Yeo, Joseph Jon-yin Wan, Sir-Young James Loh
pmc-12639215.description: Background:Autologous matrix-induced chondrogenesis (AMIC) is an effective treatment for focal chondral knee lesions. Rehabilitation optimizes the environment for cartilage healing while avoiding deleterious effects to the repair site.Purpose:To evaluate rehabilitation protocols after AMIC and its effect on clinical and radiological outcomes.Study Design:Scoping review; Level of evidence, 4.

pmc-12719052.title: Neonatal Hyperbilirubinemia in Uganda: Mechanisms, Clinical Consequences, and Health-System Challenges
pmc-12719052.creator: Mohamed Yusuf Hamdi, Jolly Nankunda, Hanan Asad Hassan, Zakaria Abdi Said, Ahmed Hassan Mohamud, Feisal Dahir Kahie, Abdullahi Mohamed Abdulla, Jawahir Ali Moalim, Maryan Ahmed Moalim, Walyeldin E M Elfakey
pmc-12719052.description: ObjectiveNeonatal hyperbilirubinemia is a prevalent condition characterized by elevated serum bilirubin levels, affecting approximately 50% of term and 80% of preterm infants. While mild cases often resolve without intervention, severe hyperbilirubinemia can lead to life-threatening complications such as bilirubin-induced neurological dysfunction (BIND) and kernicterus, resulting in permanent brain damage, developmental delays, and hearing impairment.

pmc-12800240.title: Low estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) predicts decreased all-cause mortality in critically ill patients with cardiorenal syndrome (CRS): analysis of the MIMIC-IV database
pmc-12800240.creator: Yujing Zhou, Xin Su, Yunsheng Chen, Yunhui Yuan, Haiqiang Sang
pmc-12800240.description: Most previous studies on Estimated Glucose Disposal Rate (eGDR) have been conducted in general population, with few studies focusing on critically ill patients. We investigated the predictive value of eGDR in death risk in intensive care unit (ICU) patients with cardiorenal syndrome (CRS).

pmc-12833574.title: Cancer cachexia-related monocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells impair T-cell negative selection and predict immune-related adverse events
pmc-12833574.creator: Li Wei, Ya-Qin Sun, Jian-Hua Ren, Ze-Xuan Huang, Yuan Zhang, Xiu-Qing Pang, Xiao-Tong Lv, Xiang-Yuan Wu, Yan-Fang Xing, Xing Li
pmc-12833574.description: Background and aimsCancer cachexia is prevalent in various cancers and is associated with chemotherapy toxicity. However, limited data exist on the relationship between cachexia and immune-related adverse events (irAEs). The aim of this study is to explore the correlation between cancer cachexia and irAEs and its possible mechanism.

pmc-12849100.title: Breast cancer patients’ perceptions of safety: insights from the Italian NHS
pmc-12849100.creator: Federica Morandi, Roberta Laurita, Vincenzo Nardelli
pmc-12849100.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The COVID-19 pandemic caused an unprecedented demand for immediate and far-reaching organizational change. In this context, oncological care experienced delays and routine service disruption, significantly impacting patients’ outcomes. Using a unique dataset with two data sources, 366 oncological patients and 68 Breast Unit team leaders in the Italian National Health Service, this study analyzes healthcare organizational characteristics and the role of transferred perceptions of care safety among patients with breast cancer during the Covid 19 pandemic.

pmc-13059610.title: Racial, ethnic, gender and age representation of clinical trials supporting FDA approval of cancer therapies
pmc-13059610.creator: Mingye Zhao, Yunlin Jiang, Taihang Shao, Wenxi Tang
pmc-13059610.description: BackgroundPivotal clinical trials provide the primary evidence base for US FDA oncology drug approvals; however, persistent demographic imbalances in trial enrollment may compromise generalizability and exacerbate inequities in cancer care. We quantified disparities in the representation of women, racial and ethnic minority groups, and older adults in pivotal trials supporting FDA oncology approvals and evaluated trial-level characteristics associated with underrepresentation.

pmc-13177550.title: Exploring vaccine hesitancy among citizens of the Métis Nation of Ontario: a population-based data linkage study
pmc-13177550.creator: Sarah Edwards, Keith King, Shelley Cripss, Ashok Chaurasia, Eliane Kim, Hira Khan, Kwong Kwong, Jennifer Walker McMaster, Martin Cooke
pmc-13177550.description: ke, known as the “5Cs”, on COVID-19 vaccination among Métis Nation of Ontario (MNO) citizens. The Métis people are one of three Indigenous peoples in Canada. A population-based online survey was implemented by the MNO, including the short version of the “5C” (confidence, complacency, constraint, calculation, collective responsibility) psychological antecedents of vaccination scale.

pmc-13352236.description: BACKGROUNDTransgenic crops containing Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) proteins are crucial for managing major agricultural pests such as the corn earworm, Helicoverpa zea (Boddie). The fitness of Bt resistant insects on refuge crops plays an important role in determining the rate of resistance development. Previous research has investigated the fitness costs of Cry1 and Cry2 resistance in H.

pmc-13385913.title: Co-occurring clonal hematopoiesis exhibits strong selection and high leukemia risk
pmc-13385913.creator: Kara M. Barnao, Aubrey K. Hubbard, Irenaeus C. C. Chan, Weiyin Zhou, Yasminka A. Jakubek, Giulio Genovese, Wendy S. W. Wong, Rebecca L. Kelly, Corey D. Young, Derek W. Brown, Wen-Yi Huang, Neal D. Freedman, Kristine Jones, Amy Hutchinson, Belynda Hicks, Duc Tran, Donna Arnett, Kathleen C. Barnes, Jo
pmc-13385913.description: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) and mosaic chromosomal alterations (mCAs) are two types of clonal hematopoiesis (CH) associated with hematological parameters and malignancy risk. Here we show, in genomic data from 546,090 biobank participants, that co-occurring CH (≥2 CH mutations detected) is present in 1.6% of cancer-free individuals and shows strong evidence for selection (up to 804x enrichment).

pmc-13464830.title: The Necessity and Feasibility of Implementing Regenerative Practices in Pasture-Based Beef Cattle Farming
pmc-13464830.creator: Ferenc Szabó, Gabriella Holló
pmc-13464830.description: Simple SummaryRegenerative farming is an approach that restores soil health, increases biodiversity, and improves ecosystem resilience. It reduces the environmental impact by working with natural processes instead of depleting them. Although beef production emits much fewer greenhouse gases than urbanization, industry, and other agricultural sectors, beef farmers still need to consider regenerative development for the future.

pmc-13518867.title: Phase-independent wireless data aggregation via optical in-sensor computing
pmc-13518867.creator: Shuyi Sun, Zexi Lu, Yao Wang, Zihui Liu, Zhuang Mao, Qi Shi, Fengzhi Wang, Wei Wang, Jie Jiang, Bin Lu, Haiping He, Xinhua Pan, Haoliang Qian, Zhizhen Ye

pmc-13721128.title: The WRKY transcription factor IbWRKY24 regulates flavonoid biosynthesis in sweetpotato (Ipomoea batatas [L.] Lam.) blades
pmc-13721128.creator: Jilong Gao, Ruihua Qin, Qina Lv, Peitao Chen, Chunli Wu, Rong Huang, Yulong Liu, Lina Jiang, Fan Yang, Ruican Yang, Tengfei Zhao, Yufan Fu
pmc-13721128.description: Sweetpotato (Ipomoea batatas [L.] Lam.) vines exhibit strong regenerative capacity, and their blades are rich in flavonoids, making them a promising target for nutritional biofortification. Here, we quantitatively assessed flavonoid contents and antioxidant capacities in blades from 90 genetically diverse sweetpotato genotypes. Integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses identified IbWRKY24 as a key transcriptional regulator of flavonoid biosynthesis in sweetpotato blades.
